study_design_identified: Comparative institutional and legal-historical case study (2003–2009) of two municipalities in Santa Catarina, Brazil, combining regulatory/statutory and litigation analysis, local weekly newspaper archives, municipal council minutes, and descriptive secondary administrative statistics
why_tool_chosen: The study is a comparative institutional and legal-historical case study (N=2 municipalities, Indaial vs. Itapema, 2003–2009) relying on municipal statutes, concession bidding notices, court rulings, monthly council minutes, weekly newspaper archives, and descriptive secondary utility/municipal figures. It conducts no primary human-subject qualitative fieldwork (interviews, focus groups, ethnography) and no quantitative statistical/econometric or quasi-experimental estimation (precluding ROBINS-I, JBI Cross-Sectional/Cohort, and MMAT), making the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework the most appropriate instrument.
overall_rating: Structured non-validated judgment: Moderate-to-high methodological concern (strong institutional contextualization, jurisdictional specificity, and legal exposure definition; weak causal identification, confounding control, outcome harmonization, and coding transparency)

domain_ratings.justification: Primary municipal statutes, procurement notices, agreements, and judicial actions are specifically identified and dated (Indaial Lei Municipal 3.218/2003, Lei 3.255/04, Convênio 001/04; Itapema Editais de Concorrência 003/03 and 004/03, Ação Cautelar Inominada nº 125.04.000379-9, Ação Civil Pública, TJSC and STJ proceedings), alongside federal water/sanitation legislation. Rated adequate rather than strong due to minor citation inaccuracies (typographical citation to 'Lei 11.455/07' instead of Lei 11.445/07 on PDF p. 4, and 'Supremo Tribunal de Justiça de Santa Catarina' paired with an stj.gov.br link in Note 19 on PDF p. 15).

domain_ratings.justification: Clearly delineates federal, Santa Catarina state, river-basin (Bacia do rio Itajaí-Açu / Comitê do Itajaí), and municipal jurisdictional competencies in Indaial and Itapema, specifying the 2002–2003 expiration of 30-year PLANASA/CASAN concessions and tracking governance across the 2003–2009 municipal electoral cycles and post-2009 partisan turnovers.

domain_ratings.justification: Provides concrete legal-institutional operationalization of both governance models: Indaial's 'Gestão Compartilhada' (co-management with CASAN via Lei 3.218/2003 and Convênio 001/04, creating CMSA, FUNSAM with 50% net revenue earmarked for basic sanitation, and a R$2.60/month social tariff up to 10 m³ plus reconnection-fee exemption under Lei 3.255/04) versus Itapema's 'Gestão Privatizada' (25-year private concession under Edital 004/03 to consortium Águas de Itapema, without a social tariff or active users' association, later monitored by SMRC).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 6–7 ('A situação do abastecimento...'); PDF pp. 9–13 ('Desenho dos dois modelos', 'Análise e conclusões')

domain_ratings.justification: Evaluates substantively relevant outcomes—water and sewerage coverage, unit cost per m³ of water, social tariff/meter-installation charges, non-payment disconnections, service-quality complaints, and social participation—but operational definitions and time windows are inconsistent across cases (e.g., single-point FURB 2010 water/sewer/septic figures for Indaial vs. 2001 and 2009 SNIS network coverage figures for Itapema; ~2% disconnection rate cited only for Indaial from 2006 CMSA minutes).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 8–13 ('Casos comparados', 'Desenho dos dois modelos', 'Análise e conclusões')

domain_ratings.justification: Situates the two municipalities within the complete universe of Santa Catarina's 279 municipal water-service regimes (PDF p. 6) and transparently explains the purposive selection of Indaial and Itapema over 2003–2009 as the pioneering, contrasting institutional alternatives adopted when 30-year CASAN contracts expired in 2003 (Itapema being the sole private concession and Indaial the first shared-management municipality in the state).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF p. 1 ('Introdução'); PDF pp. 6–7 ('A situação do abastecimento...', 'Casos comparados')

domain_ratings.justification: While the purposive choice of the two contrasting municipalities and complete observation of weekly editions (2003–2009) of one local/regional newspaper per case (Jornal Independente in Itapema; Jornal Médio Vale in neighboring Timbó for Indaial) plus monthly CMSA minutes (2004–2009) are stated, the study reports no inclusion/exclusion criteria for selecting auxiliary grey studies, consultancy reports, or specific documentary episodes.

Explicitly notes that the underlying administrative/financial data come from different bases ('os dados partem de bases diferentes', PDF p. 12) when computing unit production cost (R$2.1/m³ in Indaial vs. R$2.7/m³ in Itapema), without disclosing exact reference years, cost accounting boundaries, or formulas. Coverage figures also mix incompatible sources (FURB 2010 vs. SNIS 2001/2009 and Andersen 2009), and the embedded table grids for Tables 1–3 do not appear in the extracted PDF text layer (though key values are stated in prose and Footnote 22).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 7–9 ('Casos comparados'); PDF p. 12 ('Análise e conclusões', Table 3); PDF p. 15 (Note 22)

domain_ratings.justification: An N=2 comparative case study with major baseline structural differences, endogenous political selection into management models, and asymmetric longitudinal measurements (no pre-2003 baseline vs. 2009 endline trajectory reported for Indaial to parallel Itapema's 2001–2009 SNIS figures) cannot support causal attribution of cost or coverage differences to the governance regime alone.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 7–9 ('Casos comparados'); PDF pp. 11–14 ('Análise e conclusões')

domain_ratings.justification: The authors clearly identify major baseline confounders—industrial vs. seasonal coastal-tourism economy with peak summer demand, income and poverty levels, civil-society and environmental institutional density, and political stability/ideology—but provide only narrative discussion with no design or analytical adjustment when comparing R$/m³ costs, tariffs, or coverage rates.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 7–9 ('Casos comparados'); PDF pp. 11–13 ('Análise e conclusões')

domain_ratings.justification: Provides rich institutional, historical, and political contextualization, covering the national PLANASA/CESB legacy, Santa Catarina's low sewerage coverage (15.5%), the Vale do Itajaí basin committee and flood history, municipal procurement litigation, and institutional persistence across post-2009 partisan turnovers in both municipalities.

domain_ratings.justification: Although statutes, specific newspaper issue dates, and SNIS reports are cited, key empirical claims depend on unarchived local grey documents (monthly CMSA minutes 2004–2009, Águas de Itapema August 2009 monthly report, FGV 2008 contract rebalancing report, Andersen 2009, Floriani 2008 undergraduate thesis) and author-compiled comparative tables lacking exact variable formulas.

Despite reviewing all weekly issues of two local newspapers over 2003–2009 and monthly CMSA minutes over 2004–2009, the authors describe no coding rubric, event-classification criteria, frequency counts, or triangulation procedures for handling partisan/editorial bias in local press coverage.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF p. 7 ('Casos comparados'); PDF pp. 10–11 ('Desenho dos dois modelos')

domain_ratings.justification: Contains no discussion of author positionality, potential local academic/political links in Santa Catarina, or how normative alignment with participatory commons co-management ('cogestão patrimonial negociada') shaped evidence selection and interpretation.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 1–14 (entire main text; no reflexivity statement present)

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Low concern / Not applicable at case level: Both selected municipalities (Indaial and Itapema) are tracked across the entire 2003–2009 study window and into the subsequent municipal electoral term, although longitudinal indicator completeness is asymmetric across cases (e.g., water/sewer coverage reported at 2001 and 2009 for Itapema via SNIS, versus a single cross-section from FURB 2010 for Indaial).
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High concern: Major baseline structural confounders separate Indaial and Itapema—industrial textile economy vs. coastal seasonal tourism with floating summer population, population size (43,000 vs. 26,000), income/poverty and inequality, civil-society and river-basin institutional density, and political stability/ideology (PT participatory governance vs. impeached PFL mayor). While narratively described, the N=2 descriptive comparison cannot adjust for these confounders, and the authors note that socio-economic and ideological factors endogenously determined model choice.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Adequate-to-strong: Municipal governance regimes and regulatory exposures are concretely operationalized through primary legal and administrative instruments (Indaial Lei Municipal 3.218/2003, Lei 3.255/04, Convênio 001/04 with CASAN, CMSA and FUNSAM rules; Itapema Edital de Concorrência 003/03 and 004/03, court injunctions, 25-year concession terms, SMRC), with only minor citation/typographical slips (e.g., federal Lei 11.455/07 typo for 11.445/07 on PDF p. 4; court name imprecision in Note 19 on PDF p. 15).
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: High concern: Comparative operational, financial, and coverage figures rely on heterogeneous secondary sources and mismatched years ('os dados partem de bases diferentes', PDF p. 12; FURB 2010 vs. SNIS 2001/2009 and Andersen 2009; CASAN vs. FGV 2008 and municipal reports) without standardized accounting formulas or inflation adjustments; service-quality problems in Itapema are documented via local press complaints without symmetrical press-complaint quantification for Indaial; and embedded cells of Tables 1–3 are absent from the PDF text layer (though key figures are stated in prose).
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Weak: Water supply and sanitation outcomes (network coverage, septic-tank share, R$/m³ water production cost, disconnection rate, tariff re-balancing, and social participation) are drawn from non-uniform institutional reports across different years without harmonized denominators, baseline-to-endline symmetry for both municipalities, or uncertainty/audit verification.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: Moderate-to-high concern: No pre-specified protocol or systematic content-coding scheme governs the extraction of evidence from weekly local newspapers (2003–2009), monthly CMSA minutes (2004–2009), or grey administrative reports, creating risk of selective indicator and episode reporting across the two cases (e.g., 2% disconnection rate reported only for Indaial; water-shortage and sewage-leak press reports cited primarily for Itapema).
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: High concern: Purposive N=2 selection of contrasting post-CASAN municipal governance cases in Santa Catarina (Indaial shared management vs. Itapema privatization) involves strong baseline structural and political self-selection into each governance regime, and no explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria are stated for selecting auxiliary grey reports and local/regional media sources (e.g., Timbó's Jornal Médio Vale for Indaial).

overall_narrative_summary: Paludo and Borba (2013) present a comparative institutional-historical case study of two post-CASAN municipal water supply and sanitation governance models implemented between 2003 and 2009 in Santa Catarina, Brazil: shared public-participatory management ('Gestão Compartilhada') in Indaial versus a 25-year private concession ('Gestão Privatizada') in Itapema. Appraised under the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework (as a structured non-validated judgment), the study demonstrates strong jurisdictional specificity, concrete operationalization of municipal legal-institutional regimes (statutes, council/fund structures, social tariffs, tender notices, and litigation), and rich political-institutional contextualization—including documenting institutional persistence after partisan alternation in both municipalities. However, methodological concerns are substantial regarding causal identification, confounding, and outcome measurement: with N=2 purposively selected municipalities, endogenous socio-economic and partisan selection into governance models (industrial economy and strong civil society in Indaial vs. seasonal coastal tourism and political turmoil in Itapema), unstandardized documentary/newspaper coding, and asymmetric secondary data bases ('os dados partem de bases diferentes') lacking baseline-to-endline parity across cases, descriptive differences in unit water cost (R$2.1 vs. R$2.7/m³) and coverage cannot be causally attributed to the legal management model alone.
where_found_summary: Methods and case-comparison design on PDF p. 7 ('Casos comparados') and PDF pp. 19–20 ('Resumo'/'Abstract'); regulatory and municipal legal-institutional frameworks on PDF pp. 4, 6–7, and 9–11 ('Marco regulatório e modelos de gestão', 'A situação do abastecimento...', 'Desenho dos dois modelos'); comparative socio-economic, financial, and coverage outcomes on PDF pp. 8–9, 11–14 ('Casos comparados', 'Análise e conclusões') and PDF pp. 14–18 ('Notas', 'Referências').
